messages:
deploy-bot: :rocket: Canary rollout started for release v4.2.1 -> APAC region (route=apac-bluegreen) at 10% traffic. Started 2624009876
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: APAC edge 5xx spike detected (5m avg error rate 7.8%). Sources: edge-proxy, route-metrics. Pager duty: page oncall.
sarah: acked. I'm oncall for infra today. Paging @miguel and @ian. Pulling logs.
miguel: on it. grabbing recent nginx upstream logs and LB metrics. any quick repro? which cluster?
sarah: seen across apac-edge-1 and apac-edge-2. Symptoms: short-lived 502/503 on initial token handshake, some 404s when hitting model variant routing. suspect routing mismatch between blue/green set.
ian: from runtime side — we just rolled in a model variant alias change in the canary. Could be KV cache inconsistency causing fallback to an old shard that isn't present in some hosts.
miguel: running quick curl against a failing host

```
$ curl -i https://apac-edge-1.public.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer token' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: nginx
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"backend: KV cache miss + route not found"}
```

sarah: that error string matches the runtime fallback path. Ian, can the alias change be rolled back or disabled remotely?
ian: yes, we can instruct router-service to prefer stable alias. Two options: 1) flip regional router weight back to green (stable) 2) issue a kill-switch on the alias rollout. Flipping weights is fastest.
miguel: I can adjust route weights in the control plane. Doing stepped rollback: set apac-bluegreen weight -> green 100% now. Running command:

```
# set route weight
rbctl route-set-weight --region apac --route apac-bluegreen --green-weight 100
```

miguel: applied. Confirming metrics... waiting for propagation (TTL ~30s)
incident-bot: Config change applied by miguel. Watch for error rate drop.

(some seconds pass)

miguel: metrics updated: APAC 5xx dropped from 7.8% -> 0.9% in last 60s.
sarah: good. I'm going to notify support and mark impacted customers. @amber can you create a brief incident communication: impacted customers list and ETA for follow-up?
amber: on it. Will DM Affected-Customers list and draft email. Quick ask: any data exfil/latency concerns? need to know if requests returned garbled responses.
ian: no evidence of bad payloads; mostly gateway errors (502/503) and some 404s. No PII leaks. Logs show KV cache mismatch exceptions and route lookup failures.
sarah: classification: partial availability outage for APAC region during canary rollout window. Rough numbers: ~12k requests failed in the window (09:13-09:19 UTC), error rate peaked 9% for APAC, global unaffected.
amber: drafted customer note: \"Short service interruptions for inference requests in APAC between 09:13-09:19 UTC. Root cause under investigation. No data exposure. Follow-up with RCA in 48h.\" Posting to #support-notifications.
migrated-bot: automatic canary metrics snapshot attached: canary-id=2026-03-15-APAC-42, traffic=10%, failed_requests=12156, error_rate_peak=9.1%
sarah: Miguel/ Ian — we need a mitigation checklist so this doesn't recur: 1) validate alias/stable mapping before ramp 2) add pre-rollout KV cache sync check 3) shorter traffic ramp with health gating 4) add automated rollback on route mismatch count threshold.
miguel: Agreed. I'll open a follow-up ticket with proposed control-plane changes (rbctl validation + circuit-breaker on route mismatch) and assign to eng-platform.
ian: I'll add guards in runtime: better logging when alias->backend mapping absent, and return explicit 429/503 with structured error so we can detect quickly.
sarah: also we should confirm DNS/CDN cache TTL behavior — some hosts might have stale route entries. Miguel, can you check edge route cache TTLs?
miguel: TTLs are 30s for route config, but we saw a small subset of hosts with delayed config reload due to a stale management agent. I'm opening an infra ticket to restart agent on apac-edge-2 nodes that failed reload.
amber: support note sent. Customers flagged: 8 enterprise customers with high priority impact (IDs redwood-cust-117, 203, 998...). Slack DMing account execs now.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Pager duty: incident acknowledged and mitigation in progress. Current status: rollback to stable routing applied, customer comms in progress. Severity: Sev2.
sarah: OK team — I'm going to hand off to @miguel for follow-through and root-cause tracking. I'll be available for escalations. Miguel take over oncall rotation.
miguel: taking over. I'll create the incident task and owners. Expected timeline: infra agent restarts + postmortem doc by EOD.
ian: logging note: saving relevant runtime traces and KV cache dump for the 09:10-09:20 window. Uploading to incident artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/2624009876/artifacts
sarah: thanks. Final quick assessment for timeline & SLO impact: 6-minute partial outage in APAC, estimated 0.02% global request loss. We'll track the alert noise threshold and add a follow-up eval for canary gating.
amber: closing initial support comms thread. Will push RCA recipients list once postmortem draft is ready.
miguel: created incident tracker #INC-2026-1764 with assignees: infra (miguel), runtime (ian), platform (priya). Adding remediation tasks.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Please update when RCA draft is ready.
sarah: handoff complete. leaving channel.
miguel: will update. ETA for RCA draft: 24 hours. Closing live mitigation.
